The Applied Scientist will build the learning environments that let AIVista train and evaluate agents before they act in real regulated workflows. This role blends reinforcement learning research with environment engineering. You will design reward and cost functions, generate curricula and counterfactual cases, validate simulator fidelity against real operations, and develop offline, safe, constrained, and multi-agent learning methods. The Applied Scientist will develop methods that turn natural-language intent into structured, machine-checkable artifacts and use those artifacts to make AI-driven software development more verifiable, traceable, and reliable. You will work from policies, regulations, standard operating procedures, requirements, process descriptions, application programming interfaces, and code to construct formal specifications, rule ontologies, process ontologies, contracts, tests, and proofs with complete source traceability.
The work addresses two distinct assurance problems. Validation asks whether a formal artifact faithfully captures authorized intent. Verification asks whether an implementation satisfies that artifact. You will build measurable validation methods for omissions and mistranslations, integrate independent checkers and proof systems, and carry the resulting evidence through the AI-driven software development life cycle. The objective is a practical development workflow in which models may propose requirements, designs, code, tests, or proofs, while deterministic checkers, versioned evidence, and human authority determine what is accepted.

At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.
In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic

item.description:
**Description** Amazon's Stores Economics and Science (SEAS) team is looking for an Applied Scientist III to help us find global optima where others settle for local ones. You will work alongside scientists and engineers with backgrounds spanning machine learning, natural language processing, information retrieval, statistics, economics, causal inference, and optimization to lower cost-to-serve, optimize selection, and apply emerging machine learning techniques across a wide range of Stores problems — all at a scale that directly shapes how customers shop.
This is a role for someone who does not default to the most popular model but instead thinks carefully about which approach will produce the most reliable and scalable result for each problem. You will lead science initiatives end-to-end, translating complex business problems into mathematical frameworks, building large-scale algorithms, and deploying production solutions in partnership with product teams. If you want to do cross-discipline applied science that moves real metrics, we would like to talk.
Key job responsibilities
* Lead large-scale science initiatives from research through production, translating supply chain and marketplace problems into mathematical frameworks and deploying algorithms that delight Amazon customers. * Design and implement machine learning and statistical models — choosing the right method for each problem rather than defaulting to a single paradigm — and take ownership of their performance in production. * Drive your team's scientific agenda by identifying new research opportunities, proposing initiatives, and aligning with technical leadership on priorities. * Collaborate with scientists, engineers, and product teams across Amazon's Stores organization to prototype, validate, and scale solutions that accelerate partner teams' progress. * Mentor and coach fellow scientists through code reviews, design reviews, and authoring of internal technical documents and external publications.
A day in the life
You might start your morning analyzing experiment results from a model you recently deployed, deciding whether the estimates are robust enough to move to an online test. By mid-morning you are whiteboarding a new formulation with a colleague from a partner team. After lunch you review a pull request, suggesting a simpler algorithmic approach that cuts latency. Later you carve out time to write code for a prototype that tests a new idea for reducing cost-to-serve. Your work regularly moves between hands-on modeling and the collaborative work of aligning your team around a shared scientific roadmap.
**About The Team** Stores Economics and Science (SEAS) is an interdisciplinary team within Amazon's Stores organization. Our mission is to apply science and engineering to move from local to global optima in methods, models, and software. We prove concepts at small scale first, then build solutions that work at Amazon scale — and we help partner teams across the company short-circuit months of research and development. Our team includes a high concentration of Amazon Scholars, and we actively collaborate with academia.
We value intellectual curiosity, open collaboration, and thoughtful problem-solving. We encourage publishing, invest in mentorship, and support your growth as both a researcher and a builder.

* 3+ years of building machine learning models for business application experience * PhD, or Master's degree and 6+ years of applied research experience * Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language * Experience with neural deep learning methods and machine learning
**Preferred Qualifications**
* Experience with modeling tools such as R, scikit-learn, Spark MLLib, MxNet, Tensorflow, numpy, scipy etc. * Experience with large scale distributed systems such as Hadoop, Spark etc.

item.description:
**Description** AWS Elemental builds media services used by broadcasters, streaming platforms, and sports leagues to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video. Elemental Inference is the applied machine learning team within that organization. We develop models that understand and transform live and file-based video, producing capabilities such as intelligent reframing, highlight detection, video enhancement, and contextual metadata for advertising and content discovery. Our work reaches customers through the same media workflows that carry major live events, always-on channels, and large on-demand libraries.
As a Senior Applied Scientist, you will develop new machine learning approaches and carry the strongest ideas into production. Current work spans multimodal video, audio, and language models; spatial and temporal understanding; active-speaker and point-of-interest detection; scene retrieval; video super-resolution; and learned methods for improving compression. These problems rarely have a single accepted metric or a ready-made dataset. You will help define the task itself, determine what evidence is needed, and build evaluation methods that reflect the experience of people watching and working with the resulting video.
This role combines applied research with the practical demands of a real-time media service. You will design datasets and objectives, train models at scale, run controlled comparisons, and investigate failures. You will also work closely with engineers to export, optimize, and deploy those models. A result is not finished when it performs well in a notebook. It must preserve its quality after conversion, fit within GPU memory, meet latency and throughput targets, handle the temporal behavior of live video, and operate at a cost customers can sustain.
You will be a technical leader on the team as well as an individual contributor. The role calls for someone who can take an ambiguous customer problem, separate the scientific questions from the engineering constraints, and lead a team toward a defensible answer. You will review experiments and models, mentor other scientists and engineers, and improve the shared methods the team uses for training and evaluation. Strong judgment matters here. So does the ability to explain a complicated result clearly, including its limitations, to people from several disciplines.
We welcome candidates with deep experience in computer vision, multimodal learning, video processing, or related areas. Direct media experience is valuable but not required. A scientist who has solved difficult problems in another field, understands how to test ideas rigorously, and wants to learn the video domain can also succeed in this role.
Key job responsibilities
Lead the formulation of ambiguous video problems into research plans with clear datasets, objectives, baselines, evaluation protocols, and production acceptance criteria.
Develop models for multimodal video understanding and generation, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression.
Develop models for multimodal video understanding and description, spatial and temporal reasoning, detection and tracking, scene retrieval, video enhancement, and learned compression.
Build evaluations that measure the behavior customers will see. Depending on the problem, this may include task accuracy, factual support, temporal localization, retrieval quality, perceptual video quality, rate-distortion performance, or human review.
Take models from research code to production-ready artifacts. Partner with engineers on model export, reduced-precision inference, quantization, numerical parity, accelerator-specific optimization, and integration with serving systems and video pipelines.
Balance model quality against latency, throughput, GPU memory, context limits, and operating cost. Diagnose problems across training stability, data quality, precision, compilation, serving, and live temporal behavior.
Build reusable mechanisms for dataset management, experimentation, model comparison, regression detection, and performance measurement rather than solving each research problem in isolation.
Review scientific work and production code. Identify weak comparisons, data leakage, unsupported conclusions, untested edge cases, and operational risks before they reach customers.
Work with product managers, software engineers, and other scientists to make scope and design decisions. Use evidence to resolve disagreement and communicate what is known, what remains uncertain, and what further work is worth doing.
Mentor scientists and engineers in experimental design, machine learning methods, video evaluation, and production ML practices.
Contribute applied research through internal technical reports, patents, and publications at appropriate conferences or workshops.
**About The Team** AWS Elemental provides a portfolio of cloud media services built to prepare, process, deliver, and monetize video at global scale. Our technology supports some of the world's largest live broadcasts as well as 24/7 channels and on-demand content. The broader organization brings together expertise in video coding, image processing, distributed systems, advertising, and the operational demands of professional media.
Elemental Inference applies machine learning across that video pipeline. The team works on video understanding and enhancement, contextual metadata, smart composition, event detection, retrieval, and compression. Some projects use large multimodal models that combine video, audio, and language. Others use specialized temporal or spatial models designed for a narrow task and a strict real-time budget. We choose the approach that fits the customer problem rather than forcing every problem into the same model family.
Scientists on the team own more than model architecture. They build and govern datasets, develop annotation methods, train on distributed GPU infrastructure, and create evaluations that can reveal where a model succeeds or fails. They compare internal models with external alternatives and track accuracy, perceptual quality, latency, memory use, and cost. When a model is ready to ship, scientists work with engineers to convert it into a verified production artifact and integrate it into the inference service or the underlying video-processing engine.

item.title: Principal Applied Scientist, Supply Tech - Advertising - Amazon
item.description:
**Description** Amazon Ads is one of the fastest-growing advertising businesses in the world, connecting brands with hundreds of millions of customers across shopping, streaming, gaming, audio and the open web. Behind every ad that runs on Prime Video, Twitch, IMDb and thousands of external publisher apps and sites is a decisioning platform built by Amazon Ads Supply Tech.
That platform makes X trillion ad decisions every day and supports $XB+ in annual publisher revenue across XX+ Amazon-owned publishers and X,000+ external publishers in streaming TV, audio, display, mobile and podcasts. Every one of those decisions is a science problem: which inventory qualifies for which buyers, how publisher commitments are paced and delivered, which ad wins among competing candidates, and what price maximizes long-term yield. Each must be solved in milliseconds, under strict latency and cost budgets, while balancing advertisers, publishers, viewers and Amazon. At this scale, a fraction-of-a-percent model improvement is worth $X millions.
We are looking for a Principal Applied Scientist for this platform. You will decide where machine learning creates the most value, bring intelligence into real-time runtime systems, and lead models from idea to production.
As a principal, you will be a technical leader across the organization. You will raise the science bar, mentor senior scientists, and influence product and engineering leaders. You will work alongside excellent, driven scientists, engineers and product leaders who take on hard problems and invest in each other’s growth. Few places in the world operate at this scale.
Key job responsibilities
* Define the ML strategy for the ad decisioning platform. Set a multi-year science vision across pricing, yield optimization, forecasting, ad selection and commitment delivery, tied to measurable business outcomes. * Identify opportunities to deploy intelligence in runtime systems. Find where rules and heuristics in real-time serving paths can be replaced or improved by learned models, and partner with engineering to fit them within latency, compute and reliability budgets. * Build ML models that operate at X trillion decisions a day, drawing on approaches such as deep learning, reinforcement learning and bandits, causal inference, forecasting, and auction and mechanism design. * Evaluate ML models rigorously. Design offline, counterfactual and off-policy evaluations and online experiments. Define metrics that capture long-term value for advertisers, publishers and viewers, not just short-term lift. * Refine models for output quality and performance. Improve accuracy, calibration and robustness, cut serving latency and cost, and monitor models in production for drift and degradation. * Set technical standards, review science designs and launches, and mentor and grow senior and principal-track scientists. * Push the frontier, including LLM and agentic approaches, and contribute to Amazon’s internal and external science community through papers, talks and patents.
A day in the life
Start the day reviewing off-policy evaluation results for a new pricing model that projects an X% yield lift, and deciding with your team whether it is ready for an online test. Next, you work with engineers on fitting a deeper model into a millisecond latency budget at X billion requests. At midday, you dig into why a forecasting model drifted during a live sports event, and sketch a fix. Later, you review a scientist’s paper draft and present the science roadmap to product leaders. Throughout, you work with brilliant, driven colleagues who sharpen your thinking and help you grow.
**About The Team** Ads Decisioning team brings together applied scientists and product managers to build the intelligence behind Amazon’s publisher business. We serve Amazon-owned publishers such as Prime Video, Twitch and IMDb, along with thousands of external publishers across streaming TV, audio and display. Our models decide, in milliseconds, which inventory qualifies for which buyers, how commitments are delivered, which ad wins and at what price, balancing advertisers, publishers, viewers and Amazon. We pair scientific rigor with a bias for production impact, learn from each other, and invest in each other’s growth. Come solve problems few teams anywhere get to work on.
